blocks.text: Memo: Docker Compose for Woo, Kubernetes only for inventory-api

This is the working cut for LSH-MEM-2024-006 on January 18, 2024. Luis Ortega asked for a written bound after the current path (Compose for Woo, k8s for API) stopped being honest. I am Michael Gilfilian, Web Developer, writing for Luis Ortega, Cole Brennan, and Mara Singh. Primary host k8s.lakeshore.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on Helm the four Woo sites, then open questions. If you are implementing next week, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the commands or contracts.

inventory-api stays on k8s.lakeshore.internal. Woo stays Docker Compose. Reject a four-site Helm chart this quarter ($0 cash, ~6 weeks of freeze risk). I am not restating a hallway yes. Helm the four Woo sites is out because WordPress plus a cluster is a new product. Luis does not have freeze budget for a new product in Q1. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: look at sites=4, weeks=6, nodes=3, api=1, year1=0.0, freeze=Fri, plugins=22, risk=6.0. Sibling tickets LSH-5108 and LSH-SOP-2023-033. I will not reopen Helm the four Woo sites in a side thread because a vendor sent a discount. Cole Brennan is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Mara Singh owns a leftover that is easy to skip: inv-api.lakeshore.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (35): refuse on Helm the four Woo sites, lock is split runtime, no Woo-on-k8s this quarter. I will not hide a product change inside a 'quick align' on LSH-5108.
I asked if Kubernetes would make the site faster. I need a no that I can show a contractor.

What a skeptical user would try first on k8s.lakeshore.internal: the path Luis Ortega actually has, not a desktop demo. Metric I will argue is time-to-useful, not a vanity QPS. If we cannot show that path on woo-prod.lakeshore.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Michael Gilfilian will not accept a laptop screenshot as that proof.
Constraints and the lock

blocks.label: Lock
blocks.text: split runtime, no Woo-on-k8s this quarter Host k8s.lakeshore.internal. Ticket LSH-5108. Acceptor Luis Ortega.

Open clock: split runtime, no Woo-on-k8s this quarter. If that clock collides with a freeze, the date moves and the scope does not. Luis Ortega hears the new date on LSH-MEM-2024-006. I will not book a change in the last 40 minutes of a freeze because it is 'just config.' Config is a change. Host if we have to prove a count: k8s.lakeshore.internal.

blocks.text: Helm the four Woo sites is out. WordPress plus a cluster is a new product. Luis does not have freeze budget for a new product in Q1. I will not reopen it because a vendor emailed a discount.

Failure mode if we ignore the refuse: Helm the four Woo sites comes back wearing a new coat. I want that named in review notes, not rediscovered by Mara Singh on a Monday. Ticket LSH-5108. Numbers I will not 'simplify': sites=4, weeks=6, nodes=3, api=1, year1=0.0, freeze=Fri, plugins=22, risk=6.0. Same clock as the front. I will not mix clocks to make k8s.lakeshore.internal look healthier.

What I will not claim in LSH-MEM-2024-006

I will not claim Helm the four Woo sites is impossible for a competitor. I will claim we will not buy it. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host k8s.lakeshore.internal.
First useful slice for LSH-5108

First useful is split runtime, no Woo-on-k8s this quarter, not a prettier theme or a bigger box. Luis Ortega sees that slice on k8s.lakeshore.internal. If the slice needs a second product, that is a new ticket and Luis Ortega is in the thread. I will not hide it inside LSH-MEM-2024-006.
